study type: Cross-sectional survey with retrospective data collection
exposure: Permanent contraception policies in carceral institutions
Reversible contraception policies in carceral institutions
outcome: Existence of female permanent contraception policies
Frequency of postpartum permanent contraception procedures
Access to permanent vs. reversible contraception
cohort: The study participants included a convenience sample of 22 US state prison systems, 6 county jails, and women who gave birth in custody across 10 prisons and 4 jails.
finding: The majority of surveyed US prisons and jails allowed incarcerated women permanent contraception, often without formal policies, and postpartum permanent contraception procedures occurred, frequently without concurrent access to reversible contraception.
